name: Draught lager
description: Golden, crisp and refreshing. Ask the team which lager is pouring.
history: Lager takes its name from the German word for storage.
Cold fermentation and conditioning helped pale lager spread in the nineteenth century.

name: Guest cask ale
description: A changing cask selection; the bar team can confirm today’s brewery and style.
history: Cask ale continues conditioning in the cask rather than being fully finished before packaging.
Britain’s Campaign for Real Ale was founded in 1971.

name: Rotating craft IPA
description: Hop-forward craft beer. Current breweries, ABV and availability are confirmed at the bar.
history: India pale ale developed from eighteenth-century pale ales.
The story that IPA was invented in a single moment for voyages to India oversimplifies a longer history.

name: Seasonal stout
description: Roasted malt, a darker pour and a changing guest selection.
history: Stout originally described a strong beer; stout porter later became a distinct style.
Porter and stout have intertwined histories in British and Irish brewing.

name: Guest sour beer
description: A tart, fruit-led style to ask the team about.
history: Belgian lambic is a long-established tradition of spontaneously fermented beer.
Modern sour beers can use different cultures and methods, so sour does not describe a single recipe.

name: Alcohol-free beer
description: Ask for the current alcohol-free selection and check the label for its ABV.
history: Low-alcohol beer has been produced through several brewing and alcohol-removal methods.
The terms alcohol-free and low-alcohol have different definitions across countries; check the product label.

name: Mojito
description: White rum, lime, mint, sugar and soda.
history: The mojito is closely associated with Cuba.
Its precise origin is disputed; stories about a much older drink called El Draque are often repeated.

name: Negroni
description: Gin, bitter aperitivo and sweet vermouth; orange garnish.
history: The best-known origin story places the Negroni in Florence around 1919.
The Americano is a related drink that uses soda rather than gin.

name: Margarita
description: Tequila, orange liqueur and lime, often served with a salted rim.
history: Several people and places claim the Margarita’s invention.
Its name is Spanish for daisy; the drink belongs to the wider family of Daisy-style cocktails.

name: Espresso Martini
description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and espresso; a coffee-bean garnish.
history: London bartender Dick Bradsell created the drink in the 1980s.
Despite its name, an espresso martini does not use the gin-and-vermouth formula of a classic Martini.

name: Old Fashioned
description: Whisky, sugar and aromatic bitters, finished with citrus peel.
history: The Old Fashioned recalls the early formula of spirits, sugar, water and bitters.
Its name reflects drinkers asking for a cocktail made in the old-fashioned way.

name: Passion Fruit Martini
description: Vanilla vodka, passion fruit and lime. Ask the bar about its house serve.
history: The modern passion-fruit Martini style was popularised by London bartender Douglas Ankrah in the early 2000s.
A half passion fruit is a familiar garnish, although recipes and service vary.

name: B-52
description: A layered coffee, cream and orange-liqueur shooter.
history: The B-52 is generally linked to Canadian bars in the late 1970s, although accounts vary.
The familiar layered appearance comes from the different densities of its ingredients.

name: Baby Guinness
description: Coffee liqueur with a cream-liqueur top. Contains no stout in the usual recipe.
history: The name refers to the drink’s visual resemblance to a small stout.
It is normally a coffee-and-cream liqueur shooter rather than a beer-based drink.

name: Lemon Drop
description: A citrus-led vodka shooter, often with a sugared rim.
history: The Lemon Drop cocktail is commonly associated with San Francisco in the 1970s.
Its sweet-and-sour name evokes the lemon-drop sweet; the shooter is a smaller variation.

name: Mint & Lime Cooler
description: Mint, lime, soda and a little sugar; an alcohol-free mojito-style option.
history: Alcohol-free cocktails are often called mocktails, but mixed non-alcoholic drinks predate that label.
Lime, sugar and mint connect this style to the Cuban mojito family.

name: Peroni Nastro Azzurro
description: Italian-style pale lager with a clean, citrusy finish. Ask for draught or bottle availability.
history: Peroni Nastro Azzurro was launched in Italy in 1963 and named after Italy’s famous blue ribbon.
Its signature serve is designed to stay bright and crisp alongside food.

name: Guinness Draught
description: Dark, smooth stout with roasted grain and a creamy nitrogen-settled head.
history: Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000-year lease at St James’s Gate in Dublin in 1759.
The widget and nitrogen serve helped make the modern creamy draught style distinctive.

name: Thatchers Gold
description: Somerset cider with fresh apple character and a gently rounded finish.
history: Thatchers has been making cider in Somerset since 1904.
Cider apples bring tannin and aroma that dessert apples alone cannot provide.

name: Camden Hells Lager
description: London-brewed Helles lager with a dry, lightly floral finish.
history: Camden Town Brewery began in a railway arch in north London in 2010.
Helles means bright or pale in German brewing tradition.

name: BrewDog Punk IPA
description: Modern west-coast-inspired IPA with tropical hop aroma and a bitter snap.
history: Punk IPA became one of BrewDog’s best-known beers after the brewery was founded in Scotland in 2007.
IPA bitterness comes primarily from hop compounds called alpha acids.

name: Negroni Sbagliato
description: Bitter aperitivo, sweet vermouth and sparkling wine over ice.
history: Sbagliato means mistaken in Italian; the story says sparkling wine was used in place of gin by accident.
It was created at Bar Basso in Milan in the 1970s.

name: Classic Daiquiri
description: White rum, fresh lime and sugar shaken cold and served straight up.
history: The Daiquiri is named after a village and iron mine near Santiago de Cuba.
Ernest Hemingway’s famous version was much drier and stronger than the classic formula.

name: Tommy’s Margarita
description: Tequila, lime and agave nectar with no orange liqueur; bright and direct.
history: Julio Bermejo created Tommy’s Margarita at Tommy’s Mexican Restaurant in San Francisco.
Agave syrup highlights the tequila’s vegetal sweetness.

name: Cosmopolitan
description: Citrus vodka, cranberry and lime with a vivid pink finish.
history: The modern Cosmopolitan became a 1980s and 1990s cocktail-bar classic.
Its colour comes from cranberry, while citrus vodka gives the drink its lift.

name: Amaretto Sour
description: Almond liqueur, lemon and bitters with a soft, sweet-sour balance.
history: The Amaretto Sour became popular in the United States in the 1970s.
Modern bartenders often add egg white for a silky texture, though the original style did not require it.

name: Jägerbomb
description: Herbal liqueur and energy drink served as a high-energy shooter combination.
history: Jägermeister was first produced in Germany in 1935.
The mixed serve became a late-night bar staple rather than a traditional cocktail.

name: Kamikaze
description: Vodka, orange liqueur and lime in a sharp, bright shooter.
history: The Kamikaze emerged in American bars in the 1970s.
Served up it is a cocktail; served short it becomes the familiar shooter.

name: Cinnamon Fireball
description: Cinnamon whisky served chilled as a warming, sweet-spiced shooter.
history: Cinnamon-flavoured whisky became a modern liqueur category rather than an old classic recipe.
The warming sensation comes from cinnamon flavour compounds, not serving temperature.

name: Corona Extra
description: Light Mexican lager, traditionally served cold with a lime wedge.
history: Corona Extra was first brewed in Mexico in 1925.
The lime serve became a defining bar ritual outside Mexico.

name: Neck Oil IPA
description: London session IPA with tropical hop aroma and a bright finish.
history: Beavertown began brewing in Tottenham in 2011.
Session IPA means a beer designed to keep a lighter body while retaining hop character.

name: Old Mout Berries & Cherries
description: Fruit cider with berry and cherry notes; ask about bottle availability.
history: Old Mout takes its name from a New Zealand cider tradition.
Fruit cider balances apple acidity with added berry aroma.

name: Aperol Spritz
description: Aperol, prosecco and soda over ice with orange.
history: The Spritz began as a nineteenth-century northern Italian wine-and-soda serve.
Aperol’s bright orange version became a global aperitivo favourite.

name: Paloma
description: Tequila, grapefruit soda and lime with a bright, bittersweet finish.
history: The Paloma is one of Mexico’s most popular tequila highballs.
Unlike the Margarita, its signature fruit is grapefruit rather than lime alone.

name: Piña Colada
description: Rum, coconut and pineapple blended or shaken into a tropical classic.
history: Puerto Rico declared the Piña Colada its national drink in 1978.
The drink’s exact inventor is disputed between San Juan bartenders.

name: Whiskey Sour
description: Whisky, lemon and sugar, optionally softened with egg white.
history: The Whiskey Sour appeared in print in the nineteenth century.
Egg white is a later bar technique that adds body and a soft foam cap.

name: Sambuca & Coffee Bean
description: Anise-flavoured sambuca served with the traditional three coffee beans.
history: Sambuca is an Italian anise liqueur.
The three beans are often said to represent health, happiness and prosperity.

name: Tequila Slammer
description: Tequila and sparkling mixer served short with a lively finish.
history: The slam-style serve became a party-bar ritual in the late twentieth century.
The fizz changes the texture and makes the drink feel lighter than a neat pour.

name: Lucky Saint Alcohol-Free Lager
description: Hazy alcohol-free lager with gentle malt and hop character.
history: Modern alcohol-free beers use brewing and de-alcoholisation techniques to preserve aroma.
Always check the label for the exact ABV of the current serve.
